property_summary: The reentrancy guard correctly prevents nested calls to Collect; the mutant disables the guard, allowing an attacking contract to re-enter Collect and drain more Ether than its recorded balance.

After any sequence of calls, the sum of Ether in C and the locked_ flag's value together must be consistent, but the mutant disables reentrancy by setting locked_ = false instead of true, allowing an attacker to re-enter and drain more Ether than recorded.

For any sequence of Collect calls that complete successfully, the total Ether balance of contract C must be at least the sum of all Acc balances, but the disabled reentrancy guard allows a reentrant caller to drain more Ether than its recorded balance, violating this invariant.
After a successful call to Collect by address(attacker), the attacker's recorded balance in Acc must be non-negative, but the mutant allows a reentrant attacker to underflow its balance below zero.

Without reentrancy protection on Put, a reentrant caller can re-enter Put during the external LogFile.AddMessage call and cause the Put function's Ether receipt to be accounted to the same user twice (inflated balance).

The invariant that a user's balance never increases by more than the total msg.value received by the contract across all 'Put' operations can be violated when reentrancy is removed, allowing a reentrant caller to inflate their balance.

A user's balance should only increase by msg.value per Put call, but without the nonReentrant modifier, a reentrant caller can inflate their balance by re-entering Put, causing the balance increase to exceed the total Ether sent in a single transaction.

A user's unlocked balance (balance when block.timestamp > unlockTime) that can be collected must never exceed the total Ether actually sent by that user minus what they already collected, but without the nonReentrant modifier, a reentrant attacker can re-enter Put via the fallback during the external LogFile.AddMessage call, causing duplicate balance accounting and inflating the collectable balance beyond the sent Ether.

For any call to Put with msg.value > 0, the reference correctly increases the acc.balance by msg.value, while the buggy version incorrectly decreases it, violating the invariant that acc.balance must be >= msg.value after a Put when starting from 0.

After any call to Put, the caller's Acc[caller].balance must be at least the msg.value sent during that call, assuming starting from zero; the bug subtracts instead of adds, so the balance becomes less than the sent amount (and assertion in sub_uint256 may revert), violating min-balance invariant.

After a call to Put(msg.value = v) from an account with a prior balance b, the new balance Acc[caller].balance must equal b + v (the original invariant); the buggy version sets it to b - v, which for b=0 causes sub_uint256 to revert.
After any number of Puts, the sum of all Acc balances must equal the contract's Ether balance, which holds in the reference but fails in the mutant because Put subtracts instead of adds Ether.

The sum of all Acc balances in the correct contract is always equal to address(C).balance; in the mutant, an unchecked overflow in Put can cause acc.balance to wrap around, breaking the invariant that total recorded balance equals actual Ether held.

After any sequence of calls, the balance recorded for any holder never exceeds the sum of their deposits; the mutant's unchecked addition allows overflow that makes acc.balance less than a single deposit.
After a Put call, the recorded balance of msg.sender must equal the previous balance plus msg.value; the mutant uses unchecked addition that overflows for large inputs, breaking this equality.

After any Put call, the sum of msg.value over all calls from an address must equal the recorded Acc[address].balance; the mutant using unchecked addition overflows acc.balance for large msg.value, breaking this invariant.

After a Put call, the balance recorded for msg.sender is strictly greater than the balance before the call (when msg.value > 0), which holds in the reference due to checked arithmetic but fails in the mutant when an unchecked overflow wraps acc.balance to a smaller value.

After any Put call, the recorded unlockTime must be at least the current block.timestamp. The reference enforces this floor but the mutant stores an arbitrary _unlockTime that can be below block.timestamp.

For any sequence of calls to Put, the recorded unlockTime must never decrease below the block.timestamp of any subsequent Put call, which the mutant violates because it overwrites unlockTime unconditionally without enforcing the >= block.timestamp floor.

The reference contract ensures that after any Put call, the unlockTime is at least the call's block.timestamp; the mutant stores an arbitrary low value, making the balance collectable earlier than intended.

After a Put with _unlockTime below block.timestamp, the reference sets unlockTime to block.timestamp, while the mutant sets it to _unlockTime, so the public Acc mapping reveals a value strictly less than the Put call's block timestamp.

After any call to Put, the acc.unlockTime stored is always greater than or equal to the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the mutant can store a lower unlockTime, making it less than the block.timestamp of the Put call.
After Put, the string argument passed to LogFile.AddMessage must emit 'Put' in the latest History message; the mutant writes 'Wrong', violating this exact logging invariant.
After a call to Put, the Data field of the latest LogFile History entry must equal 'Put', which the reference holds and the mutant violates by setting it to 'Wrong'.
After any call to Put, the Data field of the most recent LogFile History entry must equal the string 'Put'; the mutant breaks this by storing 'Wrong' instead.
After a call to Put, the latest History entry in the Log contract (LogFile) must have its Data field equal to 'Put', which the reference satisfies but the mutant breaks by setting it to 'Wrong'.
After a successful Put call, the latest entry in the Log contract's History array must have its Data field equal to 'Put'; the mutant violates this by writing 'Wrong'.
After any single successful call to Put, subsequent calls should remain possible; the buggy modifier permanently locks, making a second Put call revert.
After calling Put, the contract must not permanently lock; a second call to Put from the same account must succeed, and the buggy version reverts on the second call due to the missing unlock.
After a successful Put, a subsequent Collect on the same holder must remain possible; the buggy modifier permanently locks, causing the Collect call to revert due to reentrancy guard.

After a successful Put call, the reentrancy guard must be released; the buggy version leaves it permanently locked, so a subsequent call with sufficient gas must succeed on the correct version and fail on the buggy one.

After a successful Put call, the reentrancy guard must be released so that a subsequent call that interacts with the same contract via fallback (triggered by a low-level call with value from a helper receiving Put funds) does not revert due to the guard; the buggy version permanently locks, causing the internally triggered Put (via fallback) to revert on the second call while the reference succeeds.

A call to Put(...) must not be re-entrant; the reference enforces this via modifier nonReentrant_, while the buggy version without the require(!locked_) check allows re-entrancy that leads to an inconsistent state where the Acc[msg.sender].balance is not simply msg.value after a single non-reentrant call.

After any sequence of re-entrant calls through Put, the Acc balance of the original caller must equal the sum of all msg.value sent, because the re-entrancy guard prevents nested calls; the mutant without the guard allows re-entrancy where the same funds are added multiple times, violating this invariant.

After a re-entrant call to Put via a contract that calls back during the Collect send, the caller's Acc balance must equal the sum of all distinct msg.value deposits, but the mutant's missing require(!locked_) allows the re-entrant Put to overwrite the caller's balance from a stale storage, causing double-accounting of the same msg.value.

A single Put call from an adversarial contract's fallback or receive function, triggered by a Collect transfer, should never be able to increase the caller's balance by more than the total value they sent; the mutant allows the re-entrant Put to add msg.value without the prior transfer being protected, breaking this invariant.

After a re-entrant Put call through Collect, the attacker's Acc balance equals only their originally sent Ether, not double-counted; the mutant without the require(!locked_) allows re-entrant Put to add msg.value before the Collect transfer reduces balance, duplicating the deposit.

After any sequence of calls to Put, the contract never becomes permanently locked (i.e., a subsequent call to Put with sufficient gas never reverts with a reason other than out-of-gas), but the buggy version using assert can cause a permanent lock due to Solidity's 0.8.x panic revert consuming all gas, making the modifier uncallable.

For any Put call after initialization, the contract never becomes permanently locked, but the buggy version using assert(!locked_) can cause a permanent lock when locked_ is true, as assert in Solidity 0.8.x consumes all gas via panic revert, making the modifier uncallable and preventing any state from being written.

For any sequence of calls to Put, the contract never loses more funds than it has received, but the buggy version uses assert which panics and consumes all gas, causing a re-entrant caller to bypass state updates and steal funds.

After a call to Put where the call fails due to the modifier's condition (locked_ is true), the balance of the caller in the Acc mapping remains unchanged in the reference implementation; in the buggy implementation using assert, the modifier panics and reverts, but if the call is made via a re-entrant adversary that catches the panic, the state changes can be applied, leading to a balance increase.

For any call to Put by an EOA, the call succeeds and increases the caller's balance by msg.value, while the buggy version using assert causes a panic revert that consumes all gas, making the call always fail.

For any call to Collect by a re-entrant attacker, the reference C's nonReentrant_ modifier prevents balance manipulation during the external call, ensuring acc.balance reflects exactly one subtraction of _am; the mutant lacks this protection, allowing a re-entrant call to manipulate the balance and cause an incorrect final acc.balance.

For any successful Collect call, if the account's balance is observed before and after, the difference must be exactly the requested amount; the buggy version allows reentrant manipulation that causes the observed balance to decrease by more than the requested amount.

After a successful Collect to a re-entrant caller, the Acc balance of the caller on C must equal the previous balance minus the requested amount; the buggy version without nonReentrant_ allows the caller to re-enter and deposit, so the final balance can be greater than or equal to the pre-collect balance.

For any successful Collect, the caller's Acc balance after the call must equal the balance before the call minus the collected amount; the mutant allows a re-entrant attacker to call Put during Collect, increasing the balance so the final balance can exceed pre-balance minus amount.
For any reentrant caller, a successful Collect in the reference always deduplicates the final acc.balance by exactly _am, while the mutant can under-deduct due to reentrancy.

After Collect succeeds, the caller's Acc balance must equal the pre-call balance minus the withdrawn amount plus any deposits made during the call; the mutant reduces balance before the call, so a reentrant deposit during the external call will cause the final balance to be off by the reentrant amount.

After a successful Collect, the caller's Acc balance must equal the pre-call balance minus the withdrawn amount; the mutant deducts before the external call, so a failing external call (revert) leaves the balance incorrectly reduced.

In reference C, after a successful external call that sends Ether in Collect, the caller's Acc balance is reduced by the withdrawn amount; the mutant reduces the balance before the call, so a successful call that fails to notify the Log contract does not change the final balance relative to pre-call minus amount, but the mutant incorrectly stores a reduced balance permanently even if the external call succeeds but the Log update reverts.

After any successful Collect, the caller's Acc balance must be reduced by exactly _am regardless of whether the low-level call succeeds or fails; the mutant reduces balance before the call, so a low-level call that returns false (but does not revert) leaves the balance incorrectly reduced while the reference restores it by deducting only on success.

After a successful Collect call, the caller's Acc balance must be reduced by the collected amount (when conditions pass); the mutant leaves the balance unchanged while still sending Ether, breaking this invariant.
